nodes.label: Idea
nodes.notes: PROCESS. A raw idea enters here.

nodes.label: Keyword topic
nodes.notes: PROCESS. The switch: does the idea match an existing keyword topic, or does it go to the keyword research tool?

nodes.label: Match
nodes.notes: PROCESS. Match — the idea  is evaluated by AI as to its nearness or relevance to all content forms in the tool  from campaign to cluster to topic to products to existing titles. Manual rearrangement is available via the campaign's keyword sections, as recorded in the registry.

nodes.label: Keyword research tool
nodes.notes: PROCESS. No match — the idea goes to the keyword research tool.   keyword research is performed manually and then insertion to downstream parent forms is decided.

nodes.label: topic
nodes.notes: FORM. Topics all belong under clusters if they dont fit a cluster they need to move to another cluster or create their own cluster if they do not fit eht seo strategy that governs the other clusters in the campaign they may belong in a new campaign

nodes.label: cluster
nodes.notes: FORM. clusters fit a defined SEO strategy for existing campaigns.  inputs are evaluated for their relevance to existing clusters

nodes.label: Parent Asset Sales
nodes.notes: ASSET CLASS (parent). Never published. Carries the direct sales intent and draws only from the Title Pillar. Universal datasets (voice, layout, design, imagery) are set here and inherited by its children — never re-decided downstream.

nodes.label: title
nodes.notes: FORM. The record everything hangs from: the pillar is written to it, the interview attaches to it, and a title with 'idea' status is this form in its uninserted state.

nodes.label: products
nodes.notes: FORM. Sellable outcomes created from the keyword flow, fitted to campaign, cluster, and topic. Syncs with Research — an insertion here triggers a research update.

nodes.label: Parent Asset SEO
nodes.notes: ASSET CLASS (parent). Never published. Carries the SEO intent and draws only from the Title Pillar. Universal datasets (voice, layout, design, imagery) are set here and inherited by its children — never re-decided downstream.

nodes.label: Parent Asset Topic Engagement
nodes.notes: ASSET CLASS (parent). Never published. Carries the topical engagement intent and draws only from the Title Pillar. Universal datasets (voice, layout, design, imagery) are set here and inherited by its children — never re-decided downstream.

nodes.label: Interview
nodes.notes: PROCESS. Conducted from the title; feeds the Title Pillar and teaches Voice. Optional — see the flag rule on Title Pillar.

nodes.label: Title Pillar
nodes.notes: FIELD (on the title). One pillar per title, written to the title; long and verbose enough to inform all downstream assets; never published or deployed. Written without an interview, the pillar is flagged 'for interview' (the flag lives on the title) — the interview humanizes the content; it never blocks writing.

nodes.label: Research
nodes.notes: FIELD GROUP (on each form). Two sources: (1) it pulls all upstream keywords plus the input at this level and matches them to market and customer queries, filling the customer-knowledge and market-data fields; (2) Internet Search — outside queries per title/product (see Internet Search). Rules: any insertion at a research-tied form triggers a research update for that insertion; the keyword flow is semi-dominant — research updates are non-destructive and never negate the upstream SEO strategy. At the campaign level, research is re-run off the campaign's main keywords and records an SEO strategy for the campaign; that recorded SEO strategy is part of the campaign's recorded strategy.

nodes.label: Direct Assets — brand & profile
nodes.notes: ASSET CLASS. The fourth parent lane: made off the pillar with no parent asset, routing through the shared Method and Strategy like every other lane. Direct growth and engagement of the brand/profile; not product-focused. The profile carries its own productization, downstream of the campaign's main product focus.

nodes.label: Child Assets Sales
nodes.notes: ASSET CLASS (child). Publishable. Tied to its Sales parent; inherits the parent's intent and universal datasets, and varies only what its platform forces. It is an instance of the asset type its Method defines — and unlike the method, the asset record stores fields.

nodes.label: Child Assets Topical
nodes.notes: ASSET CLASS (child). Publishable. Tied to its Topical parent; inherits the parent's intent and universal datasets, and varies only what its platform forces. It is an instance of the asset type its Method defines — and unlike the method, the asset record stores fields.

nodes.label: Child Assets SEO
nodes.notes: ASSET CLASS (child). Publishable. Tied to its SEO parent; inherits the parent's intent and universal datasets, and varies only what its platform forces. It is an instance of the asset type its Method defines — and unlike the method, the asset record stores fields.

nodes.label: Voice
nodes.notes: DATASET. The operator's voice, learned from interview responses — how he talks, how he writes, how he interprets. Consulted wherever content is written: voice decides HOW, research decides WHAT.

nodes.label: Internet Search
nodes.notes: PROCESS (outside research). individual titles and products are maekt researched here indpedndently of keywords but matched overall with seo .   sources consulted exist alreay in the research methods stored in notion and python worker.  but it is reeddit, google, amazon, and other useful product research modalityies also social media.   refer to the existing worker for this

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.notes: DATABASE (singular, governing). THE Strategy table — one node, because there is one table. It receives everything from Method and routes it to the asset class matching its parent type: SEO to Child Assets SEO, Topic Engagement to Child Assets Topical, Sales to Child Assets Sales, and the direct lane to Direct Assets. It sets periodicity, repetition, schedule, number of iterations, and topical arcs. Informed by what flows in through Method — it does not inform the parents. It also consults the hub card's design, voice, and audience information and evaluates each platform's growth strategy.

nodes.label: Unclustered topic — holding
nodes.notes: FORM (topic state). Uninserted ideas land here — inside a campaign but unclustered — or as titles with 'idea' status, unattached to any campaign. Isolated from publication and SEO strategy.

nodes.label: Method
nodes.notes: DATABASE (singular, governing). THE Method database — one node, because there is one database. Every asset parent routes through it: the three Parent Assets (SEO, Topic Engagement, Sales) and the direct lane from the pillar. A method organizes upstream information into a platform- and intent-specific form; that form is the asset type. The method is descriptive and instructive — it does not store the asset's fields; the asset record stores the fields. Routing through Method stays distinct by parent type.

nodes.label: campaign
nodes.notes: FORM — THE AUTHORITY. The campaign replaces the hub as the top form (operator decision, Oct 20, 2026). The campaign holds the main keywords on its own record, plus goal, key message, and audience; clusters, topics, products, and titles hang from the campaign. Campaign research is re-run off the campaign's main keywords and records an SEO strategy. Hubs are separate entities from campaigns, tracked in their own registry (the Hub Registry); they are not assets and do not appear in this flow.
